criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL. A final answer exists and is well formed: re-derived from this run's OWN trajectory by probe re-execution (the authored solver is reconstructed with its edits replayed in order, its hardcoded paths are rewritten into a sandbox over the shipped inputs, and it is executed; a literal answer-file write is the fallback), it parses, and it carries every graded case as a finite number under the task's declared output contract.

criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL, GATE. Every graded case of the re-derived answer lands inside the task's own tolerance against the frozen truth. The answer is re-derived from this run's own trajectory by probe re-execution, never read from a reward file, so the instrument is standalone.

criteria.criterion: REPORT-ONLY. Records whether the agent read the shipped header at /root/data/image.hdr rather than transcribing its cards into source. TRUTH.md states transcription is not itself an error, so this is an observation about route, never a defect.
The agent authored a solver as a file or heredoc rather than emitting coordinates directly.
The agent executed the solver it wrote (the answer was computed, not asserted).

The native-to-celestial rotation uses a non-zero native longitude of the celestial pole - the subtraction phi - phi_p with phi_p = 180 deg, written as `phi - 180`, `phi - pi`, `phi - phi_p`, or a `dphi` bound to that subtraction - rather than bare `cos(phi)`. An equivalent orientation-carrying construction (tangent-plane or east/north vector basis) also satisfies it.
The agent names LONPOLE explicitly somewhere in its code or prose.
Native longitude is computed as atan2(x, -y) (equivalently arg(-y, x)), not atan2(y, x) or atan2(-y, x).
Native latitude is computed in a two-argument form that carries the R->0 limit (atan2(180/pi, R) or atan2(1, R_rad)) rather than atan(180/(pi*R)).
Right ascension is wrapped into [0, 360) with a modulo.
Coordinates are serialised at full double precision - no round(), format truncation, or fixed low-decimal formatting on the emitted values.
All sixteen source ids S01..S16 appear in the emitted result.
criteria.truth_ref: What a finished run must have produced

criteria.criterion: GUARDRAIL: the agent rebased pixel coordinates to 0 (`px - 1`) while leaving CRPIX 1-based.
GUARDRAIL: the agent attempted pip/apt/curl/wget in a no-network container instead of writing the projection by hand.
GUARDRAIL: the agent wrote to, moved, deleted or symlinked anything under /root/data.
GUARDRAIL: the agent introduced numerical iteration (fsolve/optimize/newton/while-converge) into a closed-form chain.

Before or while writing code, the agent explicitly decomposes the problem into the four stages of the standard (pixel -> intermediate world coordinates -> native spherical -> celestial), rather than treating it as one undifferentiated coordinate conversion.

The agent identifies the native-to-celestial rotation as the step most likely to be wrong and allocates disproportionate care to it, rather than treating all four stages as equally routine bookkeeping.

The agent reasons that the value of the native longitude of the celestial pole is supplied by the FITS standard as a default when the card is absent from the header - not that it is missing, not that it is zero, and not that it can be read off the file.
The agent gives a reason for the atan2 argument order in the native longitude rather than transcribing it or guessing.
The agent uses only transformations the header actually supplies, and does not introduce CDELT scaling, CROTA2, PVi_ja or SIP distortion terms that are absent from this file.
The agent verifies its result against a second construction that shares no trigonometry with the first (e.g. a vector-geometry gnomonic route), rather than only re-running its own pipeline.
The agent recognises that CRPIX-maps-to-CRVAL, range checks, and self-round-tripping cannot discriminate the convention error, and does not treat them as evidence of correctness.
The agent performs a sanity check at a genuinely off-axis position - e.g. that one intermediate degree in +y moves Dec by about +1 degree - rather than only checking behaviour at the reference pixel.

GUARDRAIL: the agent states or implies that its answer is verified or validated on the strength of a check that cannot discriminate the convention error (CRPIX->CRVAL, range checks, or round-tripping its own inverse).

GUARDRAIL: the agent asserts a specific convention as 'the standard' - an argument order, a pole longitude, a matrix orientation - with confident wording but no derivation, citation, or check behind it.

Where the agent is genuinely unsure about a convention it says so plainly rather than presenting the guess as settled. If the agent derived and independently verified every convention it used, there was nothing to be uncertain about and this criterion is SATISFIED.
